newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN V SAMPDORIA - MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN V SAMPDORIA - MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Here is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Milan and Sampdoria who meet in Italy's serie A at the San Siro stadium on Sunday (1330 GMT):

Playing style: With return of Arrigo Sacchi, Milan have returned to tactics that revolutionised Italian soccer in the 1980s. In words of ex-Italy manager "players work in such tight spaces that they are forced to pass and think at high-speed." Signifies return to straight back-four which frequently resorts to the off-side trap, pressing in midfield and Sacchi's famous schemes to breakdown packed defences.
Milan's recent defensive frailities have often seen Sacchi field 4-5-1 formation with Cristophe Dugarry or George Weah acting as a lone striker.

Strengths: San Siro. Six of Milan's seven defeats have come away from home, while at home they have often produced dominant form of old. Witness 1-0 win over Vicenza in last appearance in front of own fans. Also, despite their disastrous league position, Milan still posses talented squad with players such as in-form Roberto Baggio and Dejan Savicevic capable of resolving any match in moment of genius.

Weaknesses: Milan's ageing squad, most of whom are familiar with Sacchi from national team or Milan's past, is struggling to adapt to high-intensity performances demanded by tactics. Against Verona last week, lethargic looking team caught three-times on counter-attack. Weak defence not helped by shell-shocked goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi.
Sacchi, revolutionary 10 years ago, must come to terms with fact most Serie A teams know exactly what to expect from his sides.

Motivation: Milan have virtually abdicated their title, but the champions lie just seven points adrift of second-place Sampdoria, and runners-up spot would guarantee the champions a free passage into next season's European Cup.

If that is not enough motivation for a team whose appetite for success is clearly on wane, then Sacchi has made no secret that there will be a purge of Milan's Old Guard at the end of the season. Every game is now trial for Milan of future.

Line-up (probable): Sebastiano Rossi; Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi, Alessandro Costacurta, Michael Reiziger; Dejan Savicevic, Marcel Desailly, Demetrio Albertini, Jesper Blomqvist; Cristophe Dugarry, Roberto Baggio.

Playing style: On paper, Sven-Goran Eriksson comes from the Sacchi school of football -- 4-4-2, zonal defence and pressing in midfield. In practice, experienced Swedish coach refuses to remain prisoner to tactics, changing the make-up of his side three times this season to cater for arrival of Argentine Juan Veron and Frenchman Pierre Laigle and inspired "discovery" of striker Marco Caparelli, plucked from youth team.

Unlike Sacchi, Eriksson has also given free-wheeling roles to talents of Roberto Mancini and Yugoslav Sinisa Mihajlovic. In attack, Mancini is the fulcrum of side, with all movements passing through him. At back, one-time midfielder Mihajlovic plays libero, covering his fellow defenders but also frequently moving into midfield to switch defence into attack. The result: tactically disciplined team and most entertaining football in serie A: 37 goals in just 18 matches.

Strengths: Mancini and Montella, or "M&M" as the Italian press have dubbed serie A's most prolific front-line. Both have 12 goals this season with Montella's opportunism complimenting Mancini's touch. But the duo's record reflects a team built for attack, from penetrating runs of half-backs Emanuele Pesaresi and David Balleri to relentless pressing of Marco Franceschetti and Laigle in midfield and Veron's vision just behind strikers.

Weaknesses: Defence. Despite Fabrizio Ferron's consistency in goal and Mihajlovic's emergence as world-class sweeper, Sampdoria's commitment to all-out attack frequently sees them caught on counter-attack. Against lowly Perugia, Sampdoria's refusal to sit on an early one goal lead saw them fall 2-1 down before triumphing 5-2.
With three players over 32 on the bench, Alberigo Evani, Fausto Salsano and Giovanni Invernizzi, there is a lack of depth to Eriksson's squad.

Motivation: While Eriksson insists Sampdoria's sole objective this season remains a place in Europe, his team lie second in the table, just four-points behind leaders Juventus, and victory over last season's champions would confirm their growing status as potential title winners. The last time Sampdoria beat Milan at the San Siro, in November 1990, they went on to win the championship.

Line-up (probable): Fabrizio Ferron; David Balleri, Sinisa Mihajlovic, Stefano Sacchetti, Emanuele Pesaresi; Juan Veron, Marco Franceschetti, Pierre Laigle; Marco Carparelli, Roberto Mancini, Vincenzo Montella.
